params.body:
Four places in the Studio that were hard to read.

**The desk: what is draft and what is live**
- Each row now starts with one label in the colour of where the piece stands: **Own work**, **Draft for the site**, **In review** or **Live on gentells.com**. Before, the state was one spaced-capital word among four ("OWN WORK · 0 SOURCES").
- The rows are compact: the title at reading size, with sources, premium and the last edit on one line under it, and the author on the right. The empty cover placeholder is gone.

**The line above a piece**
- "This piece is [for gentells.com], [draft], [free]." was a sentence of selects dressed as text, so nobody could see which words were controls.
- It is now three labelled switches: **Goes to** (Own work, gentells.com), **Stage** (Draft, In review, Live; Live is blocked with the reason while the review is not ready) and **Read by** (Everyone, Paying readers).
- After them come the citation check as a link, and a quiet **Delete**.

**The rail**
- Elements, Sources and Cover share one pattern: a heading with its count, one line on what it is for, and the actions as quiet links ("Tag elements"; "Suggest from the graph", "Add by hand"; "Upload", "From the sources", "Paste a link").
- The red button and the two rows of boxed buttons are gone.
- The image-link field opens only when asked.

**Curate, Posts**
- Titles at text size, with sources and date on the same line, and tighter rows, so 63 posts read as a list.
- The Trends list uses the same type.

Checked with `npm run build` and screenshots of the desk, the editor and Curate against mocked data.
params.title: Studio: where a piece stands at a glance, labelled switches, a calmer rail, a compact posts list
